title: Jain every day, a celiac child, a low-salt soft-food grandfather

told.family: Me Nikhil, my wife Pooja, our daughter Riya is 6, our son Arjun is 13, and my father Mahendra, he's 78.
told.cook: Sunita comes Monday to Saturday, 11 for lunch and 5 for dinner, about an hour each time. Breakfast and Sunday we do ourselves.
told.cookLimits: She makes good dal, sabzi, rotis. No fancy stuff.
told.cookTime: Breakfast we make ourselves in 15 minutes before school.
told.cookingDays: We cook all seven days; Sunday we cook ourselves.
told.kidsBreakfast: Riya has celiac disease: absolutely no gluten — no wheat, atta, maida, rava/sooji, bread, biscuits, nothing. Arjun eats anything.
told.kidsLunch: Riya takes a tiffin Monday to Friday, it must be gluten free like everything she eats. Arjun eats in the school canteen on weekdays and Saturday.
told.kidsDinner: Same food for everyone at dinner, but Riya's must be gluten free.
told.adultsBreakfast: Poha, upma, chilla, that kind of thing.
told.diet: We are Jain, every day: no onion, no garlic, no potatoes, carrots, beetroot, radish, ginger, no root vegetables at all, no mushrooms, no honey, no eggs, no meat.
told.elders: Papa had a heart attack last year: very low salt — no pickles, no papad, no namkeen. And he has few teeth left, so everything for him must be soft: no rotis, no hard or crisp food.
told.rules: Paneer not more than twice a week, it's heavy for papa.

rules.note: Jain: no root vegetables, mushrooms or honey
very low salt after his heart attack
few teeth: soft food only, no rotis or crisp food
paneer at most twice a week

expect.says: Breakfast, lunch and dinner every day
No onion, garlic, potato or any root veg, any day, anyone
Nothing Riya eats has wheat, atta, maida, rava, bread or other gluten
Riya has something she can eat at every meal she is home for
No pickle, papad or namkeen for Mahendra
Mahendra gets no roti or hard/crisp food
Mahendra has something soft at every meal
Paneer in at most 2 meals of the week
Breakfast is a 15-minute dish (no paratha, puri, vada...)
Riya's tiffin dish does not repeat
